b1.texto:
From once to quince, each number is a new word: **once, doce, trece, catorce, quince**.

From dieciséis to diecinueve everything is written together: **dieciséis, diecisiete, dieciocho, diecinueve**.

Veinte also has its own family: **veintiuno, veintidós, veintitrés…**

From treinta y uno on, it is separated with **y**: **treinta y uno**, **cuarenta y dos**, **cincuenta y tres**.

And the end: **cien**.
b2.f2.texto: There are thirty students in the class.
b2.f3.texto: There are a hundred books on the table.
b4.texto:
Notice the difference:

- **dieciséis, veintiuno, veintidós**: a single word
- **treinta y uno, cuarenta y dos**: three words, with **y** in the middle

The change happens at **treinta**: up to veintinueve everything goes together, and from there on it separates.
b5.f0.texto: Leo has brought a box of buttons to class.
b5.f1.texto: The teacher asks him to count them in front of everyone.
b5.f2.texto: At catorce he stops, breathes and goes on.
b5.f4.texto: Someone smiles when he reaches thirty-one.
b5.f5.texto: In the end there are seventy buttons spread over the table.
b5.f6.texto: Leo counts them again, now in a low voice, and this time he doesn't skip a single one.
b5.f7.texto: The teacher writes the figure on the board and says that seventy is a lot.
b5.f8.texto: He looks at the empty box and thinks that counting slowly is also a way of learning.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: from treinta on you write «y» in the middle.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Everything together only up to veintinueve.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Veintitrés is 23, in a single word and with an accent.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Up to veintinueve everything goes together: «veintitrés».
b8.frase: En la clase hay treinta alumnos.
intro: You already know zero to ten. From eleven on, some numbers are new words and others are joined together. From thirty-one to ninety-nine you write «y» between the tens and the units.
p.cien.consejo: Before a noun you say «cien»; «ciento» is used in 101 and above.
p.cuarenta.consejo: Careful: it's written «cuarenta», with u, not «quarenta».
p.cuántos.consejo: It takes an accent when it asks about a quantity.
p.dieciséis.consejo: It's the only one in its series with an accent: dieciséis, but diecisiete.
p.doce.consejo: Like «once», the c sounds like th in Spain.
p.once.consejo: It's written with c, but it sounds like th: «onthe».
p.quince.consejo: It's written with qu, but the u is not pronounced.
p.trece.consejo: Don't confuse it with «treinta», which is thirty.
p.veinte.consejo: From veinte come veintiuno, veintidós… all joined, in one word.
p.veintitrés.consejo: It's written as one word and with an accent on «trés».
p.alumnos.consejo: Plural of «alumno». Here it means the students sitting in the class.
p.traído.consejo: The accent on «í» splits the vowels: say «tra-í-do» in three clear syllables.
p.caja.consejo: The «j» sounds like a soft «h», so say «caja» as KA-ha.
p.botones.consejo: Plural of «botón». The strong beat falls on the middle syllable: bo-TO-nes.
p.colores.consejo: Plural of «color». The stressed syllable is «lo»: co-LO-res.
p.cuente.consejo: Subjunctive of «contar». After «pide que», Spanish uses this form instead of «cuenta».
p.respira.consejo: From «respirar». Say it slowly, res-PI-ra, as if you breathe between the syllables.
p.hondo.consejo: Same family as «fondo». Think of breathing all the way down, to the bottom of you.
p.continúa.consejo: The accent on «ú» marks the stress: kon-ti-NU-a, in four syllables. It comes from «continuar».
p.contando.consejo: The gerund ends in «-ando», for an action that is still going on.
p.prisa.consejo: Usually comes with «tener»: «tener prisa». The stress falls on PRI, the first syllable.
p.escucha.consejo: From «escuchar». The «cu» sounds like «k», and the final «cha» like «ch».
p.setenta.consejo: Built from «siete» with the ending «-enta», like «sesenta» and «cuarenta».
p.repartidos.consejo: The «-ido» ending marks a participle, here used like an adjective for «botones».
p.ocasión.consejo: «ocasión» ends in «-ón» with the accent. «ca» is «ka», and the stress lands on «-sión».
p.salta.consejo: Same root as «salto». The stress falls on the first syllable: SAL-ta.
p.tiza.consejo: The «z» sounds like a soft «th», and the stress falls on the first syllable «TI».
p.cifra.consejo: The «ci» sounds like «thi», and the stress falls on the first syllable: THI-fra.
p.vacía.consejo: It agrees with the feminine «caja», so it ends in «-a». The accent on «í» marks the stress.
p.comprende.consejo: From «comprender». The «pr» group is hard at first, so go slowly: kom-PREN-de.
p.forma.consejo: Feminine: «una forma», «la forma». It also means shape, the outline of something.
